passage: The Mauryan Empire was established by Chandragupta Maurya, who was guided by a brilliant advisor named Chanakya. Their capital city was Pataliputra. One of the most famous rulers of this dynasty was Ashoka. Early in his reign, Ashoka fought a brutal war against the kingdom of Kalinga. This was a massive, bloody conflict that changed his life forever. After seeing the destruction, Ashoka decided to stop fighting and instead promoted a set of moral principles called Dhamma. Dhamma was not a religion, nor was it forced upon his people; it was a way of living based on kindness, tolerance, and respect for others. To share his message, Ashoka had his teachings carved into hard stone pillars and rock surfaces. These inscriptions were permanent records meant for the public to read, as paper was not used for such royal proclamations during that time. Through these stone messages, Ashoka encouraged his subjects to live in peace and harmony, showing that a ruler could lead through compassion rather than just military force.

items.evidence: Dhamma was not a religion, nor was it forced upon his people; it was a way of living based on kindness, tolerance, and respect for others.
items.q: A villager in Ashoka's empire followed a different faith. What did Dhamma expect of him?
options: Keep his faith and be kind to others
Give up his faith and become a Buddhist
Follow the emperor's religion or be punished
Serve as a soldier in Ashoka's wars
items.explain: Dhamma was not a forced religion; it asked people to live with kindness, tolerance and respect.

wrong.why: thinks Dhamma was Buddhism that everyone had to join
thinks Dhamma was forced on people
misses that Ashoka gave up fighting

items.evidence: These inscriptions were permanent records meant for the public to read, as paper was not used for such royal proclamations during that time.
items.q: Ashoka wanted ordinary people to read his messages for many years. What did he use?
options: Hard stone that would not wear away
Paper scrolls sent to every village
Secret letters to his royal officers
Soldiers who shouted his orders aloud
items.explain: Stone inscriptions were permanent records for the public; paper was not used for royal messages then.

wrong.why: thinks inscriptions were written on paper
misses that the messages were meant for the public
thinks a ruler spreads messages only through soldiers

items.evidence: After seeing the destruction, Ashoka decided to stop fighting and instead promoted a set of moral principles called Dhamma.
items.q: Why did Ashoka decide to stop fighting wars after Kalinga?
options: He saw the terrible destruction it caused
He had lost the war against Kalinga
He had already become a Buddhist monk
Chanakya the king ordered him to stop
items.explain: Seeing the destruction of the Kalinga war made Ashoka stop fighting and promote Dhamma.

wrong.why: guesses that a king stops fighting only after losing
thinks Ashoka was a monk who ruled in peace
thinks Chanakya was the Mauryan king

items.evidence: The Mauryan Empire was established by Chandragupta Maurya, who was guided by a brilliant advisor named Chanakya.
items.q: Who started the Mauryan Empire, and what was Chanakya's role?
options: Chandragupta, helped by his advisor Chanakya
Chanakya, who ruled as the first king
Chandragupta, after Chanakya the king died
items.explain: Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire; Chanakya was his advisor, not a king.

wrong.why: mixes up the order of Chandragupta and Ashoka
picks the right founder but keeps Chanakya as king
